title: Four questions replace a single ‘accuracy’ score

name: slide-4-title
text: Four questions replace a single ‘accuracy’ score
textPreview: Four questions replace a single ‘accuracy’ score

name: lens-body-0
text: Did any predicted region cover at least 70% of both reference sides?
textPreview: Did any predicted region cover at least 70% of both reference sides?

name: lens-body-1
text: How much extra code did the prediction include? Report precision and IoU.
textPreview: How much extra code did the prediction include? Report precision and IoU.

name: lens-body-2
text: Given a match, was the region correctly attributed to T1, T2, or T3?
textPreview: Given a match, was the region correctly attributed to T1, T2, or T3?

name: lens-body-3
text: Was T4 proved by SMT, observed dynamically, or only structurally suggested?
textPreview: Was T4 proved by SMT, observed dynamically, or only structurally suggested?

text:
The 70% rule follows BigCloneEval-style c-match. Boundary precision and IoU prevent whole-file predictions from looking precise. T4 evidence tiers remain separate.

title: Three reference layers answer three questions

name: slide-10-title
text: Three reference layers answer three questions
textPreview: Three reference layers answer three questions

name: gt-question-0
text: Did the detector find the corresponding block?
textPreview: Did the detector find the corresponding block?

name: gt-question-1
text: Did it isolate the changed code and assign the right type?
textPreview: Did it isolate the changed code and assign the right type?

name: gt-question-2
text: Did unchanged code remain identifiable as Type 1?
textPreview: Did unchanged code remain identifiable as Type 1?

text:
The three references prevent one coarse label from hiding localization and type behavior. Mutation scoring is the discriminating measure; clone interval matching is intentionally reported with a localization warning.
